1 1] This appeal has been filed by the appellant-original claimant against the respondents-original opponents under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, ( 'The Act', for short) against the judgment and award passed by learned M.A.C.Tribunal (Aux.) Sabarkantha @ Himmatnagar, in Motor NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/5199/2007 JUDGMENT DATED: 17/07/2023 undefined Accident Claim Petition No. 683 of 1997 on 14.09.2005.

sentences.text:
The parties are hereinafter referred to as the claimants and the opponents as they stood in the original petition for the sake of convenience,
clarity and brevity.

2] The brief facts that emerge from the record of the case are as under:-
2.1] That on 27.04.1997, the claimant, his wife and minor son "Parth" were coming in Jeep No. RJ-06-C-0064, which was being driven by the opponent No.1, belonged to opponent No. 2 and was insured with the opponent no. 3 and when they reached near the board of village Piplodi on Prantij-Himmatnagar National Highway Road at around 01.30 p.m., the opponent No. 1 was driving the Jeep in a rash and negligent manner and the Jeep turned turtle and the claimant sustained serious injuries.
The offence was registered at Himmatnagar Town Police Station being I-C.R.No.113 of 1997.
2.2] Due to the accident, the claimant sustained serious injuries and was admitted in Civil Hospital Himmatnagar but as the injuries were grievous, he was shifted to Rajasthan Hospital, NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/5199/2007 JUDGMENT DATED: 17/07/2023 undefined Ahmedabad and he sustained injuries on his left hand, which was operated upon and amputed.

entities.text: Rajasthan Hospital, NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/5199/2007 JUDGMENT
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: That the claimant has incurred huge medical expenses and at the time of accident, he was aged 32 years and working as a junior Geologist in Gujarat Water Supply and Sewerage Board at Modasa.

entities.text: Gujarat Water Supply and Sewerage Board
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: That the claimant has sustained permanent disability and claimed an amount of Rs.3,00,000/- from the opponents jointly and severally under all available heads.

3] The opponents were duly served with the notices and the opponent Nos. 1 and 2 appeared before the learned Tribunal and filed their written statement at Exh: 15 and the opponent No.3 appeared and filed a written statement at Exh.30.

The opponent Nos 1 and 2 admitted the factum of accident but denied that the opponent no. 1 was driving the jeep rashly and negligently at the time of accident and have stated that a dog came on to the road and as it was raining, the opponent No.1 suddenly applied breaks and hence the vehicle turned turtle.

The opponent No. 3 denied all the allegations of the claim petition and has stated that the jeep is a private vehicle and does not cover the risk of a gratuitous passengers and the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/5199/2007 JUDGMENT DATED:
17/07/2023 undefined opponent no. 3 is not liable to pay any compensation.

4] Learned Tribunal,
after recording the oral as well as documentary evidences, held the opponent No. 1 100% negligent for the occurrence of the accident and considering the pay-slip of the claimant and the disability at 40%, awarded an amount of Rs.1,06,000/- with 7% interest from the date of the petition till realization to be recovered jointly and severally from all the opponents.
5] Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the said judgment and award, the claimant has filed the first appeal mainly on the ground that the appellant has sustained grievous injuries on his left hand,
Jitendrakumar Ganpatlal Modi vs Lalitkumar Jasvantkumar Vyas on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22053518/
2 which had to be amputated and the appellant has spent a huge amount for his medical treatment.

entities.text: Jitendrakumar Ganpatlal Modi vs Lalitkumar Jasvantkumar Vyas
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: That the learned Tribunal has awarded only an amount of Rs.1,06,000/- as total compensation and the disabilities of the claimant has not been properly appreciated by the learned Tribunal.

The appellant has taken medical treatment for a long time and had spent huge amount for conveyance,
special diet and attendant charges but the learned Tribunal has granted NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/5199/2007 JUDGMENT DATED: 17/07/2023 undefined only an amount of Rs. 3,000/- and as there was amputation on the left hand, the appellant has suffered great pain, shock and sufferings but only an amount of Rs.10,000/- has been awarded by the learned Tribunal, which is a very meagre amount.
Hence, the appellant has prayed to enhance the amount of compensation.
6] Heard learned advocate Mr. N.V.Gandhi appearing for the appellant-original claimant and learned advocate Mr. Dakshesh Mehta appearing for the respondent No.3.
Though served, the other respondents have not appeared.

7] Learned advocate Mr. N.V.Gandhi appearing for the appellant- original claimant has reiterated the contents of the appeal memo and has urged this Court to enhance the amount of compensation accordingly as the learned Tribunal has granted a very meagre amount to the appellant.

8] Learned advocate Mr. Dakshesh Mehta appearing for the respondent No. 3 has submitted that the judgment and award passed by the learned Tribunal is just and proper and no inference is required in the judgment and award passed by the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/5199/2007 JUDGMENT DATED: 17/07/2023 undefined learned Tribunal,
and, hence, the appeal of the appellants must be rejected.

9] From the record and proceedings of Motor Accident Claim Petition No. 683 of 1997, it appears that the claimant was traveling in Jeep No. RJ-06-C-0064 and at the time of accident, the opponent no. 1 was driving the jeep and when they reached near the board of village Piplodi on Prantij-Himmatnagar National Highway at around 01.30 p.m., the Jeep turned turtle and the claimant sustained injuries.

sentences.text: A complaint of the accident is produced at Exh. 32 and the panchnama of the place of offence is produced at Exh. 34.
As per the panchanama, the jeep was lying on its side and was damaged and the claimant has produced the medical certificates at Exh; 35.

[9.1] This certificate is of Sir Pratap General Hospital, Himmatnagar and the claimant has also produced the certificate of Rajasthan Hospital,
Ahmedabad at Exh. 36.

As per the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/5199/2007 JUDGMENT DATED:
17/07/2023 undefined certificate produced at Exh 36, an amputation below left elbow was done and the claimant has been examined on oath at Exh:
32.
The claimant, in the deposition, has reiterated the contents of the claim petition and has also produced the pay-slip at Exh:

sentences.text: 3 39 and the certificate stating the claimant did not attend his duties for 64 days at Exh: 40.

During the cross examination, it has come on record that, there was an increase in the salary of the claimant and due to the permanent disability, there was no reduction of any sort in the income of the claimant.

[10] The learned Tribunal has considered all these aspects and has appreciated the amount of future economic loss considering the disabilities of 40% of the claimant and considering that the appellant remained in hospital for about 20 to 25 days and on medical leave for 64 days, granted an amount of Rs.3,000/- towards attendant charges, special diet and transportation allowance.

Considering the injuries and the disability, the learned Tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.10,000/- as pain,
shock and sufferings.

On perusal of the medical certificates produced by the claimant and the fact that the claimant was taken to Sir Pratap General Hospital, NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/5199/2007 JUDGMENT DATED: 17/07/2023 undefined Himmatnagar and has shifted to Rajasthan Hospital,
Ahmedabad, the amount of Rs.3,000/- towards attendant charges, special diet and transportation allowance is very meagre and also considering the amputation of left hand below elbow, the amount of Rs.10,000/- granted towards pain, shock and sufferings is required to be enhanced.

Sabarkantha @ Himmatnagar in Motor Accident Claim Petition No. 683 of 1997 is hereby modified and in addition the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/5199/2007 JUDGMENT DATED: 17/07/2023 undefined claimant is entitled to Rs.32,158/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.
